title: Open a project folder
summary: Open a folder, trust it, and open a file from the Explorer.

steps.say: Make sure VS Code is the window in front. Say next when it is.
hints: Click anywhere on the VS Code window to bring it forward.
Press Alt Tab until VS Code is selected.
steps.why: Shortcuts only reach the window that is in front.

steps.say: Press Control K, let go, then press Control O to choose a folder.
hints: Hold Control, tap K, release both, then hold Control and tap O.
Or open the File menu at the top left and choose Open Folder.
steps.why: Opening a folder lets search, Git and extensions see the whole project.

steps.say: Pick a folder with a few files in it, then click Select Folder.

checks.prompt: Does the Explorer side bar now show a folder name with a list of files under it?

hints: Select the folder itself; you do not need to go inside it.
Any folder works for practice, such as Documents.
steps.why: VS Code treats the chosen folder as the project root.

steps.say: If VS Code asks whether you trust the authors, choose Yes only for your own files.
hints: If no question appears, the folder is already trusted; say next.
Choosing No opens Restricted Mode, which is safer for downloaded code.
steps.why: Trust decides whether tasks and extensions may run code from this folder.

steps.say: In the Explorer on the left, double click a file to open it in the editor.

checks.prompt: Is a file now open as a tab in the editor area?

hints: A single click opens a preview that the next file replaces; a double click keeps it.
Press Control P and type part of a file name to open it from the keyboard.
steps.why: Files you open stay as tabs so you can switch between them.
